correctness.rationale: Independent-set enumeration on the stated 30-edge graph gives (1,12,36,20) by excitation number and parity sizes 37/32. An allowed single flip reverses excitation parity, so the Hermitian Hamiltonian has off-diagonal block B(t) and kernel dimensions 37−rank B and 32−rank B. The separate exact replay /workspace/branches/6b9550e8-81ba-4479-87d4-d4f79216bb25/icosahedron_check.py reconstructs the graph and block, matches every Gram characteristic coefficient at t=1 by integer traces and Newton identities, and symbolically reproduces the ordered maximal minor 2(t²−1)^6. The Gram polynomial has a zero of order six and all the displayed remaining factors have nonzero constant terms, giving rank 26 and nullities 11 plus 6. The identity det(xI−H)=x⁵ det(x²I−BᵀB) yields the entire stated homogeneous polynomial. The minor forces rank 32 at every real t other than ±1, including t=0. Multiplication of each basis state containing vertex 0 by −1 conjugates t to −t, so the homogeneous rank returns at −1. The five-mode lower bound applies to arbitrary real amplitudes by parity dimensions; the full sharp classification holds only for this single-site profile and ideal projected zero-detuning dynamics. Frozen scripts were read, not executed; the uniform rank and all-real-t classification do not depend on modular sampling.

value.rationale: The icosahedron is a canonical Platonic interaction graph and a local drive defect is a meaningful perturbation of the homogeneous constrained Hamiltonian. The exact polynomial and all-real defect classification separate parity-protected multiplicity from twelve fine-tuned zero modes, rather than just reproducing the known independent-set count or a floating-point gap. These data are useful benchmarks for symmetry and sensitivity in constrained finite dynamics and do not assert physical zero modes away from perfect blockade and zero detuning.
